scope: independent semantic-diversity adjudication only; no topic edits
rubric: Прямой и обратный вопросы одной связи (Темза–Лондон), а также проверенные человеком почти одинаковые вопросы ... не считаются достаточным разнообразием: одна карточка заменяется независимым фактом.

cards.prompt: Какой минерал можно разделить на тонкие блестящие пластинки?
Какое свойство создаёт у слюды тонкие ровные листочки?

candidateAdjudication.relation: Both cards test the same mica-sheet cleavage relation: mica splits into thin, flat sheets because cleavage follows weak interlayer planes. The first asks for the mineral given the cleavage behavior; the second asks for the property given the same behavior in mica. This is the reverse/near-identical relation pattern described by the rubric, despite different answer strings and difficulty labels.
candidateAdjudication.sourceSupportDoesNotResolveDiversity: Earle pp. 46–47 and 53 support the cleavage facts in both cards. Verified correctness does not make the second card an independent fact.
candidateAdjudication.recommendation: Replace one main prompt/key with an independent mica/mineral fact (for example, a source-supported hardness, composition, or occurrence question) while retaining only if its six fields meet the normal gates. Do not apply a general template ban.
candidateAdjudication.historicalContext: The independent-geology-pilot.json records the earlier six-field PASS for mica-sheets before this pairwise diversity adjudication. That field-level source/content PASS remains historical context; this pairwise ruling makes mica-sheets ineligible to count as a distinct item until resolved.
